newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods continue to fall with demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods continue to fall with demand.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices continued to fall Wednesday, pressured by rising inventories as floodwaters in the northern half of California kept motorists off the roads, traders said.
On Tuesday, American Petroleum Institute's weekly stock report showed PADD V West Coast gasoline stocks up 705,000 barrels and distillates up 177,000 barrels on the week.
"Demand is way off and that's why we had such a big build," a broker said.

CARB-grade gasoline in San Francisco Los Angeles eased against Los Angeles grades, with bids at 77 cents a gallon, or two cents below Los Angeles. Los Angeles grade fell a cent below yesterday's levels to 79/80 cents.
Premium grades in both markets was four cents higher.
With demand weak, sellers dominated the market with offers, traders said.
"The APIs seem to have brought out more seling interest," a dealer said.
